document.title: Talking Points Regarding Usama Bin Ladin for the DCI's 2 September 1998 SSCI Briefing
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: CIA talking points for the DCI's 2 September 1998 briefing to the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. Cited in 9/11 Commission Report Chapter 4, Endnote 102.

persons.name: Usama Bin Ladin
persons.role: Leader of a terrorist organization (al-Qa'ida); indicted; target of CIA rendition/capture planning
persons.status_detail: Alive as of 2 Sep 1998; subject of a planned capture/rendition operation

mentions.quote: knows more about Usama Bin Ladin than any other top tier terrorist organization.
Bin Ladin has been indicted, and most of the information pertinent to that action was acquired by CIA.
Bin Ladin's organization and its terrorist allies. is certain after a capture operation

organizations.name: Central Intelligence Agency
organizations.notes: Author of the talking points; claims most information underpinning the Bin Ladin indictment was acquired by CIA; designed and practiced a rendition operation.

organizations.name: Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
organizations.notes: Recipient of the DCI's 2 September 1998 briefing.

organizations.name: Director of Central Intelligence
organizations.notes: Briefer to SSCI; talking points prepared for the DCI.

organizations.name: Department of Justice
organizations.notes: Listed as high-level participant/contributor to the Bin Ladin effort.

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Referred to as Bin Ladin's organization and its terrorist allies; retaliation against US interests expected.

events.description: DCI briefing to SSCI on Usama Bin Ladin, for which these talking points were prepared.
CIA rendition operation to bring Bin Ladin to justice was designed, practiced and ready to go.
A CIA rendition operation to capture Bin Ladin was designed, practiced and ready to go.
Bin Ladin was indicted. The year is inferred from the 1998 document date.
The DCI briefed the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence on Usama Bin Ladin, using these talking points.

relationships.detail: CIA designed and prepared a rendition/capture operation targeting Bin Ladin, ready by May 1998.
relationships.quote: rendition operation was· designed, practiced! ... ready to go in May 1998.

relationships.detail: DoJ participated at a high level in the effort.
NSA contributed at a moderate level.
DoD contributed at a low level.
FBI contributed at a low level.
Bin Ladin is referred to as head of the organization expected to retaliate.
relationships.quote: Bin Ladin's organization and its terrorist allies

relationships.detail: The Intelligence Community, and CIA in particular, holds more information on Bin Ladin than on any other top terrorist organization; CIA acquired most of the information behind his indictment.
relationships.quote: most of the information pertinent to that action was acquired by CIA.

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin's organization is described as having terrorist allies that would join in retaliation.
relationships.quote: organization and its terrorist allies. is certain after a capture operation

relationships.detail: DoJ made a high-level contribution to the Bin Ladin rendition operation.
NSA made a moderate contribution to the Bin Ladin rendition operation.
DoD made a low-level contribution to the Bin Ladin rendition operation.
FBI made a low-level contribution to the Bin Ladin rendition operation.

key_claims: CIA asserts the Intelligence Community knows more about Bin Ladin than about any other top-tier terrorist organization.
Most information underlying Bin Ladin's indictment was acquired by CIA.
A CIA rendition operation to capture Bin Ladin was designed, practiced and ready in May 1998.
Other agencies' contributions: DoJ high-level, NSA moderate, DoD and FBI low-level.
Retaliation by Bin Ladin's organization and its allies is certain after a capture operation, successful or not.
Terrorist attacks on U.S. interests are certain whether or not an operation is run.
